_meta.name: Cadence Agile DoR/DoD (synthetic validation fixture)
_meta.note: DEC07 Q11/Q12's third framework fixture. Fictional, not KenAddme content (DEC03 licensing unresolved, REQ-014). Marked a validation fixture, NOT a shipped starter template, per Q12's own instruction that it stay one 'until it has passed its own review' -- seed_starter_frameworks.py skips it for that reason, so it never reaches a tenant as a starter.
_meta.why_this_shape: Q11 chose an agile framework with no gates deliberately, as the harder test: 'if the rule engine and data model survive that without a special case, the model is genuinely general.' The three existing fixtures are all gate-based and all declare the same house vocabulary ('Complete', 'Approve'/'Hold'/...), so none of them could ever have tested whether a template's declared vocabulary is actually honoured.
_meta.deliberate_non_conformance: This fixture declares its OWN statuses ('Met', not 'Complete') and its OWN decision outcomes ('Increment accepted', not 'Approve'). That is the point, not an oversight: the engine hardcodes the literal English words, so this fixture demonstrates the gap rather than hiding it by conforming. See backend/tests/test_dec07_q11_agile_fixture.py and the 'DEC07-Q11 vocabulary indirection' row in docs/DEFECT_REGISTER.md. Do not 'fix' this file by renaming its statuses to 'Complete' -- that would delete the finding.
_meta.model_concessions: Two places the agile shape had to bend to the model, both recorded rather than smoothed over: (1) 'gates' cannot be empty (min_length=1), so the three recurring check sets are expressed AS gates -- a renaming, so 'no gates at all' holds in the framework's language but not in the model's; (2) GateDefinition.sequence is required, so 1/2/3 are supplied even though these checks are not an ordered run -- definition-of-ready and definition-of-done recur per story and increment-review per increment, on different cadences, not one after another.
_meta.recurrence: Each sprint is a new occurrence of the same check set (GateOccurrence.sequence 2, 3, ...), which the model already supported with no change. That is the part of Q11's generality claim that genuinely held.

gates.name: Definition of Ready
gates.description: A recurring check, applied to work entering an increment -- not a checkpoint the project passes once. Re-run every sprint.

rules.guidance: An item is ready when at least two of these hold: it states how it will be judged done, it produces something you can show, and its dependencies are known.
rules.evidence_example: The story's own acceptance-criteria checklist, linked from the board.

rules.guidance: Say plainly whether anything unknown would stop this item mid-sprint. If something would, it is not ready yet -- that is a normal answer, not a failure.
rules.evidence_example: A one-line note: 'No blocking unknowns -- auth library already proven in the last increment.'

rules.guidance: Record a rough size. Advisory on purpose: an unsized item is a smell, not a stop.

gates.name: Definition of Done
gates.description: The recurring check that finished work is genuinely finished. Re-run every sprint, against that sprint's own evidence.

rules.guidance: Link the run that passed, not a screenshot of it -- a link can be re-checked later, an image cannot.
rules.evidence_example: A link to the passing pipeline run for the merge commit.

rules.guidance: Link the review itself. Someone other than the author needs to have actually looked.
rules.evidence_example: A link to the approved review on the change.

rules.guidance: Only applies when the change alters behaviour someone outside the team can see. Internal refactors skip this.
rules.evidence_example: 'Updated the API reference and the changelog entry for the new export parameter.'

rules.guidance: Note anything you know broke and chose to accept. Advisory because recording a known regression honestly is better than hiding one to keep a check green.
rules.evidence_example: 'Export ordering changed; accepted, noted for the next increment.'

gates.name: Increment Review
gates.description: An increment-level check, called when the team holds its review -- deliberately all triggered, so it is never auto-created at project start the way the per-story checks are.

rules.guidance: Record that the increment was actually shown to someone outside the team, and to whom.
rules.evidence_example: 'Shown to the two pilot teams; notes in the review doc.'

rules.guidance: Link where the feedback landed, so the next increment's readiness check can reach it.
rules.evidence_example: A link to the review notes or the newly raised items.
